summary: Both r1 NEEDS_DISCUSSION items are substantively closed. (1) Schema v3->v4: completely and consistently fixed at every site in the document (summary, semantics table, Runtime section, AT-2939, AT-2941, changelog); independently reverified against the live tree including the M3.17 bump attribution, which is exactly right. (2) LOC cap: reconciled using my own r1-measured ~2745 comparable-subset figure and the correct mechanism (subtract the barrier-hazard proof M3.20 explicitly does not build); the top-line 2745-700=2045-to-2000-cap arithmetic is self-consistent, and I independently re-measured five of the table's per-file 'M3.2 comparable actual' entries against real `git diff --stat` output -- all matched closely or exactly, confirming the table is genuinely re-derived rather than asserted. I did find one isolated arithmetic inconsistency: the typecheck.rs row's comparison cell ('~731 incl. ~700 barrier proof SHEDS -> comparable ~230') doesn't arithmetically parse (731-700=~31, not 230), and my own line-level recount of the real M3.2 diff suggests the true barrier-specific share is closer to 250-350 lines than 700. This is cosmetic, however -- it lives in an explanatory comparison column and does not change the Coder-facing target(1600)/cap(2000), which are independently verified to sum correctly from the table's own 'M3.20 est.' column. The three new r2 ATs (2942 bidirectional collision, 2943 nested-decl rejection, 2944 const-OOB) are correctly scoped and I confirmed no contradiction between the S5.1 nested-decl REJECT rule and the shipped S10 histogram example (the example declares at top level and only uses the array inside loops, which is explicitly the permitted pattern). Recommend a one-line fix to the S12.2 typecheck.rs comparison cell before Coder for document hygiene, but nothing here rises to a blocking design concern -- APPROVE.
